summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted after an MRI revealed a new right portal vein thrombosis. He was asymptomatic and hemodynamically stable. He was started on intravenous heparin and transitioned to warfarin, achieving a therapeutic INR of 2.7 by discharge. A transient rise in creatinine, likely due to contrast from a CT scan, resolved with adjustment of his diuretic regimen. His pleural effusion showed improvement, and he remained free of infection or bleeding complications. He was discharged home with warfarin for at least three months, continued management of cirrhosis and HCC, and new prescriptions for inhalers as part of his transplant evaluation, with outpatient follow-up planned for INR monitoring and a bubble echocardiogram.
